maya: heads up — saw steady memory growth on qwen-mqa long-context nightly (100k tokens) even after we hit the usual kv cap. looks like slab fragmentation + kernel fallback interplay

ranjit: can you paste the run id / commit? any repro script?

maya: run: nightly-qwen-mqa-longrun-2026-03-16 commit: 0a9f5b2. repro script: ./tests/long_context_kv_repro.sh --model qwen-mqa --tokens 100000 --batch-profile mix. attaching short profiler output below

maya: ```
[perf] total_alloc_pages=152384
[perf] kv_active_pages=121912
[perf] kv_free_pages=30372
[perf] frag_ratio=0.248
[perf] slab_arena_count=6
[perf] arenas=[24512,20480,20480,20480,1220,1020]
[perf] kernel_fallbacks=73
[perf] avg_batch_size=1.9
```

sophia: frag_ratio ~25% is high but not catastrophic. kernel_fallbacks=73 is suspicious. were we switching kernels due to varying sequence lengths?

maya: yes — batching heuristics end up mixing short and very long reqs; kernel selector sometimes falls back from optimized MQA kernel to a generic path, which seems to scatter small slab frees across arenas. long-run steady-state shows free pages never coalesce.

zack: quick thought: do we observe per-thread arena pinning? if small frees are returning to different arenas we get internal fragmentation that stays as unusable gaps.

maya: heap map shows alternating arena use. i dumped a simplified allocator map:

maya: ```
arena0: used=24512 free=1200
arena1: used=20480 free=20480
arena2: used=20480 free=20480
arena3: used=20480 free=20480
arena4: used=1220 free=0
arena5: used=1020 free=0
```

anya: that looks like a few arenas mostly full and others completely fragmented. do we have a compact/defrag path on the KV pager?

ranjit: not currently. we rely on eviction + reuse. pager only coalesces contiguous free pages but allocations are page-aligned and small reclaim holes don't get reused across kernels if they request different page sizes (GQA vs MQA page sizing).

sophia: ah — MQA requests smaller pages in some ops but when we fallback to generic kernel it allocates larger blocks. mismatch in page-size class -> cross-arena wasted space.

maya: repro pattern: sequence of long-generation requests (uses MQA fast path) then occasional short completions that trigger generic kernel. observed cumulative growth ~ +2.1GB over 12h.

zack: perf-bot, any correlating traces?

perf-bot: @here detected elevated kernel_fallbacks on nightly-qwen-mqa-longrun-2026-03-16 between 03:10-07:40 UTC. mean latency jitter +18%. attached trace id trace-20260316-0314

maya: i captured a small syscall-level snapshot:

maya: ```
mmap(addr=..., length=65536, prot=rw) = 0x7f8c...
munmap(addr=..., length=4096) = 0
mmap(addr=..., length=4096, prot=rw) = 0x7f8d...
// lots of small unmaps then medium mmaps -> fragmentation over glibc arenas
```

anya: could be glibc arena heuristics interacting with our allocator. are we using jemalloc or system malloc in that build?

maya: system malloc. we wanted minimal diff for nightlies.

ranjit: two short-term mitigations: 1) force a single kernel choice for the run (disable fallback) to keep allocations uniform; 2) run with jemalloc/explicit arena configs to ensure same arena reuse. long-term: add a compaction pass in pager and unify page size buckets across kernels.

zack: i can try a canary with fallback disabled and with jemalloc on the same nightly image. can we also add metric for 'arena_crossfragment_pct' and track it?

maya: yes please. also instrument per-kernel page-class allocations.

ranjit: another idea: on long-context workloads, encourage batching heuristic to prefer homogenous batch composition (group very long seqs together) — reduces kernel churn. could be a cheap scheduling change.

sophia: agree — batching policy tweak + telemetry will tell us if fragmentation drops. if not, compaction is next.

maya: thanks all. will run two canaries: (A) fallback disabled + system malloc; (B) fallback enabled + jemalloc. post results here tomorrow. :rocket:

zack: nice. if A eliminates growth we can roll a short-term config change for Dedicated customers with similar workloads.

anya: logging note: add a compact_hint metric when free span > X and fragmentation > Y so we can trigger offload/defrag in non-blocking way.

maya: noted. last: does anyone know if qwen-mqa uses a different kv page alignment than mistral/llama? that could explain model-specific hotspots.

ranjit: qwen-mqa uses 64B cache lines for some kernel microallocs; llama/mistral tend to align 128B. i'll dig into the kernel glue.

sophia: great thread. please attach the two canary logs and the arena_crossfragment graph once ready. :thumbsup:
